items.title: [Bug]: VLLM silently ignores falsey yaml configuration options
items.body:
### Your current environment

[vllm-env.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30833301/vllm-env.log)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

  --config <file>.yaml silently drops boolean false values, defeating any flag whose real default isn't False

  vLLM version: v0.25.1 (vllm/utils/argparse_utils.py)

  Summary

  When loading engine args from a YAML file via --config, any key with value false is silently omitted from the resulting arg list — instead of being translated into an explicit "off" signal. This is silently wrong for any boolean-valued CLI flag whose actual default is
  not already False (e.g. tri-state fields defaulting to None and resolved later by other logic). The user has no way to know their false was ignored: no warning, no error, config just quietly reverts to whatever the flag's real default resolves to.

  Root cause

  FlexibleArgumentParser's config-file-to-argv conversion (vllm/utils/argparse_utils.py, in the loop that builds processed_args):

```
  for key, value in config.items():
      if isinstance(value, bool):
          if value:
              processed_args.append("--" + key)
          # else: nothing is appended — False is silently dropped
      ...
```

  This assumes every boolean flag's true off-state is "flag absent." That's correct for store_true-style flags defaulting to False, but wrong for flags backed by a tri-state bool | None = None field that gets filled in later by unrelated defaulting logic.

  Confirmed affected flags

  1. --enable-flashinfer-autotune → KernelConfig.enable_flashinfer_autotune: bool = None. Left unset, it's later defaulted by the active --optimization-level preset (vllm/config/vllm.py, OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL_TO_CONFIG) — O0 defaults it to False, but the overall default
  optimization level is O2, which defaults it to True. Result: enable-flashinfer-autotune: false in a --config yaml is completely ignored at O2 (the default), and flashinfer's autotune warmup (kernel_warmup.py → flashinfer_autotune → _dummy_run) still runs. In our case
  this caused a reproducible OOM during warmup across many separate debugging sessions before we traced it back to this.
  2. --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager → SchedulerConfig.disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager: bool | None = None, similarly resolved later by several auto-disable heuristics in VllmConfig (platform support, chunked local attention + eagle, KV connector HMA support, etc.).
  disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager: false in a --config yaml is dropped the same way. In our testing this one happened not to change the resolved value (the heuristics independently resolved to the same default), but it's the identical defect.

  Minimal repro

  # config.yaml
  model: <any model>
  enable-flashinfer-autotune: false

  vllm serve --config config.yaml

  Effective config (from startup log) shows enable_flashinfer_autotune=True, not False.

  Impact

  Silent — no error, no warning. Anyone using --config yaml (rather than raw CLI flags) to explicitly disable a flag whose real default isn't False will have that setting silently ignored, with no indication anything went wrong. We burned a significant amount of debugging
  time treating the resulting OOM as a memory-tuning problem before finding the actual cause.

  Workarounds

  - Wrap the field in its corresponding JSON-blob CLI arg instead of the bare top-level key — dict-valued yaml keys go through a different (correct) path that JSON-serializes the value as-is: kernel-config: '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}' instead of
  enable-flashinfer-autotune: false. Same technique already works for e.g. compilation-config: '{"pass_config": {"fuse_allreduce_rms": false}}'.
  - Or pass the flag on the raw CLI (--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune if such a negated form exists) instead of via --config.
  - Or pick an --optimization-level whose preset default already matches what you want (has broader side effects on compilation/fusion settings, not a targeted fix).

  Suggested fix

  For a boolean yaml value of False, don't just omit the flag — either emit an explicit negated form (--no-<key>) if the argparse action supports it, or otherwise ensure the config loader is aware of each flag's actual "no-op" state instead of assuming it's always False.

  ---

items.title: [Bug]: cpu_offload_gb silently no-ops on Model Runner V2 — offloader never installed, model loads fully on-GPU with no warning
items.body:
### Your current environment

Verified two ways (details in the bug description):

- **Static + unit-level:** current `main` at commit `8d9b52f7c2514490bdadfd5eb0c931e58625df2e` (2026-08-07).
- **Runtime:** RTX 5090 (SM120, 32 GB), driver 610.57.04, Ubuntu 24.04, rootless podman. Runtime observations were made on a recent vLLM build (2026-08-04 vintage) and on the v0.25.1-era code; the responsible code is unchanged on current `main` (file/line references below are to `main`).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`--cpu-offload-gb` (UVA weight offloading) — and the prefetch offload options — are **silently ignored** whenever the V2 GPU model runner is active. No offload happens, no warning is printed. For the workloads that need offloading in the first place (model bigger than VRAM), the visible failure is an OOM whose message suggests unrelated remedies (`lower --gpu-memory-utilization`, `increase --tensor-parallel-size`), so users have no hint that their offload setting never took effect.

Because several architectures now **default** to the V2 runner (`DeepseekV2ForCausalLM`, `Qwen2MoeForCausalLM`, … in `DEFAULT_V2_MODEL_RUNNER_ARCHITECTURES`, `vllm/config/vllm.py`), a plain

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --cpu-offload-gb 12
```

hits this today without any V2 flag being set — the documented `cpu_offload_gb` recipe ("virtually increase your GPU memory") breaks silently for those models.

#### Root cause (current `main`, commit `8d9b52f7c2`)

- `vllm/model_executor/offloader/base.py` — the global offloader singleton starts as `NoopOffloader`; it only becomes real via `set_offloader(create_offloader(offload_config))`.
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:980` — the **only** call site of `set_offloader(...)`, in the **V1** runner's `__init__` (V1 also calls `get_offloader().post_init()` at the end of `load_model`).
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` (V2) — never calls `set_offloader`, so `make_layers()` (`vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py:812`) wraps layers with the noop and every parameter stays on GPU.
- `VllmConfig._get_v2_model_runner_unsupported_features()` (`vllm/config/vllm.py:2288`) does not list weight offloading, so default selection does not fall back to V1, and `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` does not raise.

Notably the V2 cudagraph utilities already call `get_offloader().sync_prev_onload()` / `join_after_forward()` around capture/replay (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`) — the sync hooks exist, only the installation is missing.

There is also currently no test exercising `cpu_offload_gb` end-to-end (`grep -r cpu_offload_gb tests/` only hits config-level code), which is presumably how this went unnoticed.

#### Empirical demonstration (unmodified vLLM, same image, same command, only the runner toggled)

Qwen3.5-4B-FP8, `cpu_offload_gb=2`, `enforce_eager`, RTX 5090; recent build where this model runs on either runner:

| `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` | "Total CPU offloaded parameters" log line | "Model loading took" |
|---|---|---|
| `1` (V2) | **absent** | **5.35 GiB** (full model on GPU) |
| `0` (V1) | `Total CPU offloaded parameters: 2.01` | **3.29 GiB** |

Both runs generate; the V2 run gives no indication whatsoever that the requested offload never happened.

And the damaging default-selection case (DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat BF16, 29.26 GiB checkpoint, 31.4 GiB visible VRAM, `cpu_offload_gb=12`, main-code Python): the engine logs `Using V2 Model Runner`, then `Model loading took 29.35 GiB` — no offload line — and dies OOM in the first forward, while the identical invocation pinned to the V1 runner logs `Total CPU offloaded parameters: 12.13`, loads with **17.21 GiB** on GPU, and works. (First observed in the field 2026-08-04: 4/4 identical OOMs with DeepSeek-V2-Lite until `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`.)

#### Suggested fix

Two options, in increasing order of scope:

1. **Fail safe / fail loud (PR attached):** report weight offloading as unsupported in `_get_v2_model_runner_unsupported_features()`. Default selection then falls back to V1 (where offloading works) with the existing "Model Runner V2 does not yet support …" warning, and forced V2 raises a clear error instead of silently not offloading. Verified: with this change the DeepSeek-V2-Lite case above logs the fallback warning, offloads 12.13 GiB, and loads with 17.21 GiB instead of 29.35 GiB.
2. **Feature parity:** wire `set_offloader(create_offloader(self.offload_config))` + `post_init()` into the V2 runner as V1 does — the V2-side graph sync hooks are already in place. This needs its own validation (capture/replay with UVA views, prefetch hooks under the V2 forward), so I kept it out of the minimal PR, but happy to help test it on this hardware.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: Kimi-K3 with --kv-cache-dtype fp8 is unusable on H200/Hopper — assertion demands use_prefill_query_quantization, but that flag is silently ignored on non-Blackwell devices
items.body:
## Summary

Serving **Kimi-K3** with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` on **H200 (Hopper, SM 9.0)** fails at runtime with an assertion telling the user to enable `--attention-config '{"use_prefill_query_quantization": true}'`. **Setting that flag does not resolve the error** — the same assertion fires again. On any non-Blackwell (non-capability-100) device the flag is silently ignored, so the error is circular and unsatisfiable on Hopper.

## Environment

- **vLLM:** nightly (`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`); code line references below are from `main` @ `bc4e425883` (2026-08-06).
- **Model:** `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (nvidia MLA path, `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/mla.py`).
- **Hardware:** 4 nodes × 8× **H200** (Hopper, compute capability **9.0**).
- **Serve flags (relevant):** `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--attention-backend FLASHMLA`, `--moe-backend humming`, `--all2all-backend deepep_v2`, `--tensor-parallel-size 8`, `--enable-expert-parallel`.

## Error

```
ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1029] AssertionError: Kimi-K3 fp8 KV cache requires an fp8 prefill query; enable --attention-config '{"use_prefill_query_quantization": true}'.
```

Adding `--attention-config '{"use_prefill_query_quantization": true}'` to the serve command does **not** fix it; the identical assertion still fires.

## Root cause

The assertion at `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/mla.py:700-704` requires `fp8_prefill` (prefill query dtype == fp8) for a plain `fp8` (non-`fp8_ds_mla`) KV cache:

```python
elif is_quantized_kv_cache(self.kv_cache_dtype):
    assert fp8_prefill, (
        "Kimi-K3 fp8 KV cache requires an fp8 prefill query; enable "
        "--attention-config '{\"use_prefill_query_quantization\": true}'."
    )
```

`fp8_prefill` derives from `q_data_type`, decided in `determine_prefill_query_data_type` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py:1807-1848`):

```python
use_fp8 = (
    is_quantized_kv_cache(vllm_config.cache_config.cache_dtype)          # True for "fp8"
    and vllm_config.attention_config.use_prefill_query_quantization      # True (flag set)
    and backend_supports_prefill_query_quantization()                    # <-- False on H200
)
if use_fp8:
    return fp8_dtype
elif vllm_config.attention_config.use_prefill_query_quantization:
    logger.info_once(
        "Unable to perform FP8 prefill attention when"
        " use_prefill_query_quantization is enabled. ..."
    )
    return model_dtype   # <-- returns bf16 => fp8_prefill = False => assertion fires
```

`backend_supports_prefill_query_quantization()` (`mla_attention.py:1541-1566`) returns `False` on Hopper for **two** independent reasons:

```python
if not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100):   # H200 is SM 9.0 -> False, returns early
    return False
...
return backend_cls.get_name() in ("FLASHINFER", "TRTLLM_RAGGED", "TOKENSPEED_MLA")  # FLASHMLA not in list
```

`is_device_capability_family(100)` is `(current_capability // 10) == (100 // 10)`, i.e. **Blackwell (SM 10.x) only**. H200 (SM 9.0 → `90 // 10 = 9 != 10`) fails immediately, before the backend check.

**Net effect:** on H200 (and any non-Blackwell device / unsupported prefill backend), `use_prefill_query_quantization=true` can *never* make `q_data_type` fp8, so the Kimi-K3 plain-`fp8` KV-cache assertion is unsatisfiable. The user is instructed to enable a flag that has no effect on their hardware — a circular error with no escape path from the message itself.

## Expected behavior

Any one (ideally the first) of:

1. **Fail fast with an accurate message at config-validation time**: reject `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` for Kimi-K3 when the device is non-Blackwell or the prefill backend isn't in the supported set, and point users at `fp8_ds_mla` (bf16 prefill query) or a supported backend/device — instead of a misleading runtime assertion that recommends an ineffective flag.
2. The Kimi-K3 assertion message (`mla.py:701-704`) should reflect the actual device/backend gate (Blackwell + FlashInfer / TRT-LLM Ragged / TokenSpeed), not recommend `use_prefill_query_quantization` unconditionally.
3. `determine_prefill_query_data_type` should **warn or raise** when `use_prefill_query_quantization=true` but the device/backend can't honor it, rather than silently downgrading to `model_dtype` and letting a downstream assertion fire.

## Workaround (for other users hitting this)

Use `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla` (DS-MLA fp8, 656B per-tile self-scaled) instead of `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`. That branch (`mla.py:681-699`) uses a **bf16 prefill query** (it asserts `not fp8_prefill`) and works on Hopper without any prefill query quantization. Drop `--attention-config '{"use_prefill_query_quantization": true}'` when switching.

labels.name: mrv1-only
labels.description: Issues/PRs which apply only to Model Runner V2 (not applicable to Model Runner V2)

items.body:
The reason for making this change to legacy MRV1 is that we're planning to turn on nan checking by default for all CI tests, and we don't want it to effectively disable async scheduling for most of them that (for now) still run using MRV1.

VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS made _bookkeeping_sync do `logits.isnan().sum(dim=-1).cpu()` on the main stream, one blocking D2H per step. That defeats async scheduling, whose whole point is to keep the step free of host syncs. V2 already avoids it: the counts stay a device tensor and are copied on the async output copy stream, with the dict materialized only after the copy event is synchronized.

Do the same under async scheduling: hand the device tensor to AsyncGPUModelRunnerOutput, which copies it alongside sampled_token_ids and builds the dict in get_output() after
async_copy_ready_event.synchronize().

Sync scheduling is left reading the counts back inline. That path already blocks elsewhere in the step, so there is nothing to gain from staging the copy, and leaving it alone keeps the diff small.

Behaviour is unchanged: test_raise_on_logit_nans passes on both the v1 and v2 params, NaN injection is still detected under both scheduling modes, and test_get_nans_in_logits needs no modification.

See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50323

items.title: [Bugfix] MiniMax-M3: structured output silently ignored with thinking enabled (scheduler reasoning-end gate never fires)
items.body:
## Purpose

Structured output (`response_format: json_schema` / `json_object`) is **silently ignored** for MiniMax-M3 whenever thinking is enabled (`chat_template_kwargs: {"thinking_mode": "enabled"}`): the server returns HTTP 200 with unconstrained prose. Cause: the scheduler's structured-output gate can never observe the end of reasoning.

`StructuredOutputManager.should_advance` calls `is_reasoning_end_streaming` on its request-local parser. `MiniMaxM3ReasoningParser.is_reasoning_end_streaming` early-returns `False` while `_reasoning_active_streaming` is set — but that flag is only ever cleared by `extract_reasoning_streaming`, a frontend/detokenizer method the scheduler never calls. With `thinking_mode: "enabled"` the flag initializes `True`, so:

- detection never fires → `reasoning_ended` never latches,
- `should_fill_bitmask` stays `False` forever → the grammar never engages,
- the request completes normally, making the failure invisible to clients.

Related failure family: #34650, #39130 (reasoning gates silently disabling structured output).

## Fix

Evaluate the reasoning-end predicate over the token history **before** the frontend streaming-state early return.

Two subtleties, both encoded in the regression tests:

1. **Ordering, not containment.** `input_ids` spans prompt+output, and the M3 chat template's `<thinking_instructions>` block embeds literal `<mm:think>` / `</mm:think>` text inside the prompt. A naive "history contains end marker" check fires at step 0, engaging the grammar immediately — which suppresses thinking entirely and (because no `</mm:think>` is ever emitted) makes the frontend parser classify the whole JSON as `reasoning`, leaving `content` empty. The correct predicate is `is_reasoning_end`'s ordering rule: last end marker *after* last start marker — the template's trailing `<mm:think>` prefill keeps it `False` until the model truly closes the block.
2. **Incremental scan.** The scheduler calls this per token; a full-history `rfind` per call is O(history) and measurable on long-context requests (M3 supports 1M). The parser now caches the last-seen marker positions and scans only unseen tokens (with a marker-length overlap), resetting if the sequence shrinks (fresh stream reusing the parser).

Frontend streaming extraction is unchanged — the state flags still gate the adaptive-mode heuristics; once a block truly ends, the marker check fires identically to before.

## Verification

- 27/27 parser unit tests, including 5 new regression tests: scheduler calling pattern (single-token deltas), spec-decode-style multi-token windows, **prompt-scaffolding marker text**, split-marker incremental scan, scan-cache reset. The scheduler-pattern and scaffolding tests fail on the unpatched parser.
- Live end-to-end on a production TP8 B300 deployment (v0.25.1 overlay) serving MiniMax-M3 with EAGLE3 speculative decoding (`num_speculative_tokens: 3`): before the fix, 10/10 `thinking + json_schema` requests returned unconstrained markdown; with this fix (combined with the pre-commit boundary filter — see note), 10/10 returned schema-valid JSON in `content` with genuine reasoning in `reasoning`, streaming and tool calling intact, spec decode confirmed active via `/metrics`.

## Note on speculative decoding

This fix makes the boundary *detectable*; under spec decode the boundary step can still commit post-marker tokens sampled before the mask engaged. #43424's pre-commit grammar filter handles that leak — the two compose (without this fix, that filter can never trigger for MiniMax-M3, since detection is what arms it). On v0.25.1-era code we also needed the exact boundary index stored at pre-commit time; on main, #43388's `new_token_ids`-based window in `should_advance` already provides the equivalent.

Happy to add the observed-but-preexisting cleanup separately: `accept_tokens` logs `ERROR ... Please file an issue` for draft-token rejections that the reasoning-boundary bitmask path explicitly tolerates — a dry-run `validate_tokens` in that path would silence expected noise.

items.title: Step3p5ReasoningParser strips the wrong newline
items.body:
Fixes #51164 

## Purpose
Step3p5ReasoningParser.extract_reasoning called the base parser and then applied content.removeprefix("\n") to strip the stray newline the model emits right after </think>. This only works because the base parser currently discards any text before <think>, so content is always exactly content_after.

Once #50918 lands, the base parser preserves that prefix by prepending it to the content. The returned string becomes content_before + content_after, and removeprefix("\n") then strips the leading newline of content_before while the newline after </think> survives — two errors at once.

## Fix

extract_reasoning now partitions internally (start token, then end token) instead of post-processing the base result, mirroring the approach already used by MiniMaxM3ReasoningParser. The newline trims are applied to the reasoning tail and content_after specifically; content_before is preserved verbatim and never has a newline stripped. This makes the parser correct independent of whether #50918 has merged.

## Test Plan
python -m pytest tests/reasoning/test_step3p5_reasoning_parser.py -v

Regression test change 
The existing non-streaming NEW_LINE case ("\n<think>...</think>\nThis is the rest") previously expected content "This is the rest" — the leading "\n" was dropped only because the base parser discarded the prefix. Under the preserve-prefix semantics that expectation is updated to "\nThis is the rest", consistent with the "\nIntroAnswer" example in the issue. This is deliberate, not a regression.

items.title: [Bug]: --enable-prefix-caching is a silent 0%-hit no-op on Mamba-2/GDN hybrids (Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration)
items.body:
## Summary

On `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` (arch `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`, Mamba-2/GDN hybrid), serving with `--enable-prefix-caching` yields **0% prefix-cache hits even for requests sharing a long identical prefix**. The recurrent conv+SSM state isn't prefix-cacheable (APC tracks attention KV blocks), so `--enable-prefix-caching` is effectively a **silent no-op** — callers expect shared-prefix prefill reuse and don't get it.

## Repro / measurement

Serve with `--enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 4096`. Fire request A (~561-token prompt as token IDs, `max_tokens=1`); wait 2 s (staggered, not concurrent); then request B = A's exact token IDs + a short suffix. Read `/metrics`:

```
vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total  1131
vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total     0      -> 0% hit
```

Staggering rules out the "concurrent requests race before the cache populates" explanation — the hybrid's recurrent state simply has no APC entry.

## Ask

Is this known? Ideally `--enable-prefix-caching` would either (a) warn that it's a no-op for hybrid SSM/Mamba models, or (b) support caching the recurrent state.

## Environment / caveat

vLLM **0.26.0**, GB10 / sm_121a. Not re-verified on current `main`. Found with an AI agent (Claude Code).

items.title: [Bug]: Step3p5ReasoningParser strips the wrong newline once the discarded prefix is preserved (follow-up to #50918)
items.body:
### Your current environment

Code-level report against `main`; no runtime environment required. The affected
path is pure Python string handling.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**This is a latent issue: it does not reproduce on `main` today.** It becomes
real once #50918 merges. Anyone testing current `main` will correctly see nothing
wrong, so please read the "why it is not visible yet" section before closing.

Raised during review of #50918 by @nikJ13, confirmed by @suryansh29, and split
out here on his suggestion so the fix in #50918 can stay narrow.

#### The interaction

`Step3p5ReasoningParser` post-processes the base class's return value
(`vllm/reasoning/step3p5_reasoning_parser.py`, lines 95-105 on `main`):

```python
def extract_reasoning(self, model_output, request):
    reasoning, content = super().extract_reasoning(model_output, request)
    if reasoning is not None:
        reasoning = reasoning.removesuffix("\n")
    if content is not None:
        content = content.removeprefix("\n")
    return reasoning or None, content or None
```

The intent is documented a few lines below, in the streaming path: *"Drop the
immediate newline that models often emit after `</think>`."* So the strip targets
the beginning of the text that follows the end token.

Today the base class returns exactly that, and the strip lands correctly.

After #50918 the base returns `content_before + content_after`, where
`content_before` is text the model produced *before* the start token. When that
prefix is non-empty, two things go wrong at once:

- the newline the strip was meant to remove is no longer at index 0, so it survives
- the newline now at index 0 belongs to `content_before` and is removed instead

#### Worked example

For `model_output = "\nIntro<think>reasoning</think>\nAnswer"`:

```text
content_before = '\nIntro'
content_after  = '\nAnswer'

intended                    -> '\nIntroAnswer'
main today                  -> 'Answer'          (correct; no prefix exists to lose)
after #50918, then Step3p5  -> 'Intro\nAnswer'   both errors visible
```

#### Why it is not visible yet

On `main` the base discards `content_before` entirely — that discard is the bug
#50918 fixes. With the prefix gone, `content` always starts with the newline that
follows `</think>`, so `removeprefix("\n")` does the right thing by accident. The
misalignment only appears once the prefix is preserved, which is why no existing
test covers it.

#### Scope

`step3p5` is the only subclass of `BaseThinkingReasoningParser` that
post-processes newlines. Checked on `main`:

| parser | own `extract_reasoning` | newline handling |
|---|---|---|
| `deepseek_r1` | no, uses the base | none |
| `hy_v3` | yes, returns `super()` unchanged | none |
| `ernie45` | yes, calls `super()` then extracts `<response>` | none |
| `minimax_m3` | yes, full override | none |
| `step3p5` | yes, calls `super()` then strips | **only one** |

That rules out lifting the newline logic into `BaseThinkingReasoningParser`: it
would silently change three parsers that do not strip today. `ernie45` is the most
sensitive, since it documents its expected shape as
`abc\n</think>\n\n\n<response>\n...`.

Worth stating separately: applying `removeprefix("\n")` to `content_before` is not
correct in any location. That text precedes the tag; its leading newline has no
"artifact after `</think>`" justification, and removing it is the same class of
silent loss #50918 is fixing.

#### Suggested fix

Give `step3p5` its own partitioning, the way `minimax_m3` already does, so the
newline logic lands on `content_after`:

```python
def extract_reasoning(self, model_output, request):
    if self.start_token in model_output:
        content_before, _, after_start = model_output.partition(self.start_token)
        reasoning, end_found, content_after = after_start.partition(self.end_token)
        if not end_found:
            return reasoning.removesuffix("\n") or None, content_before or None
        content = content_before + content_after.removeprefix("\n")
        return reasoning.removesuffix("\n") or None, content or None
    return super().extract_reasoning(model_output, request)
```

This touches no other parser. I have not run it against the step3p5 tests, so
treat it as a sketch rather than a patch.

#### What I did not verify

- The streaming path (`extract_reasoning_streaming`) has its own newline handling
  at lines 115-122 and 163. I have not checked whether #50918 affects it.
- I have not reproduced this at runtime, because it cannot be reproduced until
  #50918 lands. The analysis above is code-level and the worked example was run
  against both versions of the base-class logic in isolation.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I have searched existing issues and could not find this reported.
- [x] I have made sure the reproduction is minimal and self-contained.

items.title: [Bug]: OffloadingConnector can silently return wrong output at exact chunk boundaries with mamba_cache_mode=all
items.body:
### Your current environment

Reproduced with:

- vLLM: `0.25.1` nightly, commit `752a3a504`
- Model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2` (hybrid full-attention + Mamba)
- `enable_prefix_caching=True`
- `mamba_cache_mode="all"` (the model's default when prefix caching is enabled)
- `OffloadingConnector`, CPU KV offload enabled
- eager execution, greedy decoding

The relevant condition is still present in v0.26.0 and current `main` (`43c4bdcae9e589fde99984d1d5d03cbdeecf716b` as checked on 2026-08-05), although I have not rerun the GPU reproduction on those revisions yet.

### Describe the bug

`OffloadingConnector` can silently produce different output after a CPU-cache refetch when the prompt length is exactly a multiple of the offloaded Mamba chunk size and `mamba_cache_mode="all"`.

`resolve_mamba_align_size()` currently enables hit-window alignment only for `mamba_cache_mode == "align"`:

```python
if isinstance(kv_spec, MambaSpec) and kv_spec.mamba_cache_mode == "align":
    ...
```

However, `"all"` mode also stores recurrent Mamba states at token/block positions. A prefix lookup is capped at `num_tokens - 1` because the final token must be recomputed for logits. At an exact chunk boundary, without alignment the offload lookup can therefore return `N - 1` tokens while restoring the state stored at boundary `N`. That state already contains token `N`, so recomputing token `N` from it applies the token twice and changes the output without raising an exception.

### Reproduction

1. Create an `LLM` with the configuration above.
2. Use a deterministic token prompt whose length is exactly two offload chunks. In this model/configuration the chunk size was 1408 tokens, so the prompt length was 2816.
3. Generate once with greedy decoding to populate the CPU offload cache.
4. Clear the GPU prefix cache while retaining the connector cache (`reset_connector=False`; on the tested revision the default reset retained it).
5. Generate the identical prompt again.

Observed:

```text
cold:    prompt=2816 cached=0    first tokens=[18631, 43085, 17091, 47695, 1556]
refetch: prompt=2816 cached=2815 first tokens=[18631, 43085, 17091, 47695, 1270]
```

The engine completes normally, but the fifth generated token differs.

With the one-line change below, the refetch is rounded back to a valid recurrent-state boundary (`cached=1408` in this setup) and the generated output is bitwise identical to the cold run:

```diff
- if isinstance(kv_spec, MambaSpec) and kv_spec.mamba_cache_mode == "align":
+ if isinstance(kv_spec, MambaSpec) and kv_spec.mamba_cache_mode in ("align", "all"):
```

### Expected behavior

A CPU-offloaded prefix hit must never resume from a recurrent state that already includes the token being recomputed. Cold execution and CPU-refetch execution should produce identical greedy output.

### Suggested regression test

The existing `test_mamba_align_cpu_offload` already tests exact-boundary and mid-block prompts, but explicitly sets `mamba_cache_mode="align"`. Parameterizing the boundary case with `"all"` should cover this failure.

### Related but separate issue

#46453 tracks per-group prefix-hit divergence for hybrid Mamba models. This report is specifically about offload hit-window alignment in `mamba_cache_mode="all"` at an exact chunk boundary.

No error or warning is raised at load time. Root cause: `transformers`' own `Mistral3Config.__init__` (the top-level composite-wrapper config class) hardcodes `tie_word_embeddings: bool = True` as its own signature default and never reads/syncs it from `text_config` -- while `Ministral3Config` (the nested `text_config` class actually used for the language model) independently defaults to `tie_word_embeddings=False`. These are two different classes with two different hardcoded defaults, so any checkpoint whose `config.json` doesn't explicitly pin both fields (e.g. the pristine base model itself) loads with a latent conflict between them -- before any merge/export/fine-tuning is involved. `transformers`' own weight-tying logic uses `text_config` (confirmed: `transformers.generate()` is coherent, and the checkpoint's `lm_head.weight`/`embed_tokens.weight` are verifiably distinct tensors, see below), so the top-level field is functionally vestigial there and the mismatch is invisible to `transformers` itself. vLLM appears to resolve tying from the top-level field instead, silently discards the checkpoint's real, correctly-trained `lm_head.weight`, and computes output logits through `embed_tokens.weight` instead -- explaining the exact symptom (valid vocabulary, incoherent output) with no load-time error, since a redundant `lm_head` tensor under an assumed-tied model is normally dropped silently by vLLM's weight loader rather than flagged. ## Environment - vLLM 0.25.1 - Checkpoint: HF-format LoRA-merge of `mistralai/Ministral-3-8B-Base-2512` (`architectures: ["Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration"]`, `model_type: "mistral3"`, nested `text_config.model_type: "ministral3"`) - Reproduced under both vLLM's native `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration` implementation and `model_impl="transformers"` (the generic Transformers-modeling-backend fallback) -- **identical** gibberish output under both, including in `enforce_eager=True` mode (CUDA graphs ruled out). This points to the bug being in something vLLM's engine does identically across both model-implementation backends (weight-tying resolution), not in either backend's own forward-pass/kernel code. ## Relevant config.json fields ```json { "architectures": ["Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration"], "model_type": "mistral3", "tie_word_embeddings": true, "text_config": { "model_type": "ministral3", "tie_word_embeddings": false, ... }, ... } ``` The base model (`mistralai/Ministral-3-8B-Base-2512`) itself has no `tie_word_embeddings` field at either level in its raw `config.json` -- the conflict above only becomes visible once the config is loaded into Python objects (`Mistral3Config`/`Ministral3Config`'s differing defaults fill it in) and then re-serialized, e.g. by a LoRA-merge/export step's `save_pretrained()` call (LLaMA-Factory's `llamafactory-cli export` in our case). That serialization step isn't introducing the conflict -- it's faithfully writing out a conflict that already exists in `transformers`' own class defaults for this model family, latent in the base model from the moment its config is parsed. So this isn't specific to merged/fine-tuned checkpoints: any HF-format Mistral3/Ministral3-family checkpoint without both fields explicitly pinned could hit this in vLLM. ## Verified NOT the cause (ruled out before landing on this) - **Corrupted/incomplete merge weights**: `transformers.generate()` on the identical checkpoint is coherent. - **Weights silently left at random init / silently-skipped checkpoint tensors**: checked `vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py`'s `DefaultModelLoader` and `AutoWeightsLoader` -- both raise `ValueError` if any model parameter never receives a checkpoint tensor, or if an unexpected/unmapped checkpoint tensor doesn't match a model parameter (unless explicitly allowlisted, e.g. `.bias`). Loading succeeds without error here, so this isn't a plain missing/unmapped-weight situation. - **CUDA graph / kernel-fusion corruption**: reproduced identically with `enforce_eager=True`. - **RoPE (YaRN) `rope_parameters` handling**: this checkpoint's `text_config.rope_parameters` uses `rope_type: "yarn"` with `mscale`/ `mscale_all_dim` fields vLLM's YaRN implementation doesn't extract (confirmed via `vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/__init__.py`'s `get_rope()` allowlist) -- flagged and tested as a hypothesis, but injecting a corrective `attn_factor` (computed to cancel the resulting ~1.277x default mscale back to the reference implementation's 1.0) produced byte-for-byte near-identical gibberish, ruling this out as the (or at least the primary) cause. - **vLLM's own `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration` implementation specifically**: `model_impl="transformers"` (bypassing vLLM's hand-written `mistral3.py` entirely) reproduces the identical output. ## Confirmed: lm_head and embed_tokens are genuinely untied in this checkpoint ```python from safetensors import safe_open import torch with safe_open("model-00001-of-00004.safetensors", framework="pt") as f: lm_head = f.get_tensor("language_model.lm_head.weight") embed = f.get_tensor("language_model.model.embed_tokens.weight") torch.equal(lm_head, embed) # False (lm_head.float() - embed.float()).abs().max().item() # 0.32110595703125 ``` ## Fix that resolves it (tested) Patching only the top-level `tie_word_embeddings` field to match the nested `text_config.tie_word_embeddings` (leaving everything else, including the actual weights, untouched) fully resolves the issue. Validated end-to-end: ran the same checkpoint through a full production evaluation harness (37 real judge-classification datasets, full sample counts, not a toy subset) both before and after the patch -- before: uniform incoherent gibberish regardless of dataset; after: real, varied, discriminating metrics (accuracy 0.65-1.0, F1 0.46-1.0, sensible TP/TN/FP/FN splits) closely matching a known-good `transformers.generate()`-based baseline run on the same checkpoint/datasets. ## Suggested root-cause fix For composite VLM wrapper classes like `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration`, `vllm/model_executor/models/mistral3.py`'s `__init__` already passes `hf_config=config.text_config` (not the top-level composite config) when constructing the inner language model via `init_vllm_registered_model(...)` -- i.e. vLLM already treats `text_config` as authoritative for that submodel's architecture/layer construction. Whatever resolves the weight-tying decision for that inner language model should be consistent with this and also read `tie_word_embeddings` from that same `text_config`, rather than (apparently) falling back to the top-level `vllm_config.model_config.hf_config.tie_word_embeddings`. items.title: [Model] Kimi-K3: all requests degenerate to a repeated token after long-context prefill (NaN logits; packed KDA prefill suspected)
items.body:
# Summary

Serving `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` at long context reproducibly degenerates: once a large-context request (~240K tokens, well inside the model's 1M-token spec) is processed, the deployment begins returning a **single repeated degenerate token on every step for every subsequent request**, never samples EOS, and every request runs to `max_tokens`. In the observed incident the state persisted ~19 hours and the set of corrupted requests grew over time (2 → 8 concurrent), i.e. the corruption **spreads between requests and is permanent per request** until process restart.

We have proven the logits go NaN (see below); what remains open is *where* the NaN originates. This issue is filed as an investigation-in-progress with the evidence, two ready-to-run repro tests, and a concrete suspect code path — AI assistance was used in the investigation and in preparing this report.

# Proven mechanism (established from the live system, not inferred)

- The emitted token id is **0** every step. `KimiK3Config` sets `pad_token_id = 0`; chat deltas render empty (special token skipped) while `/v1/completions` renders ` @`.
- Constant index-0 output means `greedy_sample` (`vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py:240`) returned argmax over NaN logits (argmax over NaN resolves to index 0).
- Confirming evidence: while debugging, a logprobs request against this deployment killed the (Rust) frontend with `token_ranks must be >= 1 for decoded engine-core logprobs`. The rank is computed as `(logprobs >= sampled_logprob).sum(-1)`; that count can only be 0 when the sampled logprob is NaN (all IEEE-754 comparisons against NaN are false).

# Environment

- Image `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k3`, `max_model_len=256000`
- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1`, `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`
- Prefix-cache hit rate measured 0.0% throughout the incident
- (A `collect_env.py` re-run from the affected pod is pending; happy to attach.)

# Why this looks like an implementation bug, not a model limit

- 240K ≪ the 1M context window in the K3 tech report.
- The vLLM K3 port is very new (~7 commits in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/`; `kda.py` has two) and is registered outside `vllm.model_executor.models` (`registry.py:466`), the shape of an in-progress vendor drop (`[Model] Add Kimi K3 support: model files and kernels [1/N]`).
- `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1` bypassed the usual length guard.

# Hypotheses checked and eliminated

| Candidate | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Stale KDA state-slot reuse | **Ruled out.** `gather_initial_states` masks on `has_initial_state` and zero-fills fresh sequences (`gather_initial_states.py:35-40`). |
| CUDA-graph padding rows writing into a real state slot | **Ruled out.** Padding gets `NULL_BLOCK_ID = 0` (`backends/utils.py:46`); block 0 is the reserved null block (`block_pool.py:190`). |
| Batch-wide activation quant scale (one Inf token poisoning a shared `amax`) | **Ruled out.** MXFP4 `sf_block_size = 32` blocks run within a token along `hidden_size`/`intermediate_size` (`mxfp4.py:298-322`) and apply to routed expert weights only (`model.py:1224`); no cross-token reduction. KDA itself stays bf16. |
| Numerical overflow from the paper's decay design | **Weakened.** The report's BF16-safety argument (p.5) depends on `g_min = -5` and 16-token tiles; both match the port (`_KDA_GATE_LOGBOUND_MIN = -5.0` at `kda.py:52`, `BC = 16` at `chunk_intra.py:482`). The designed margin is intact. |

# Live hypothesis: packed KDA prefill leaks across sequences

`vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/kda.py:658`: when a batch contains **even one** prefill, that branch handles *everything* — decodes included — packed into a single `_flashkda_prefill` / `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` call via the whole batch's `cu_seqlens` (`kda.py:285`, `605`), with `initial_state` gathered for every sequence (`kda.py:692`; `has_initial_state` true for running decodes per `kda_metadata.py:407`).

So a NaN-poisoned running request shares one kernel launch with every freshly arrived request, and `kda.py:732` writes results back to the state cache — making infection permanent per request. A poisoned set that can only grow matches the observed 2 → 8 spread and 19-hour persistence.

**Unproven link:** whether NaN actually crosses sequence rows inside that kernel. A correct packed kernel respects `cu_seqlens` and keeps sequences independent; FlashKDA is a compiled extension (`vllm._flashkda_C`) with a shared `workspace` for inter-CTA reduction (`kda.py:190-196`) — a plausible place for a tile scheduler to span sequence boundaries, but not readable from Python. The alternative that cannot yet be excluded is NaN weights, in which case the batching story is irrelevant.

# Repro plan (tests written; need a CUDA run)

Two tests for `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py`:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py \
  -k "leak_across_sequences or state_threading" -v -s
```

- **`test_packed_prefill_does_not_leak_across_sequences`** — three packed sequences, NaN injected into the middle one's `initial_state`; assert sequences 0 and 2 are unchanged vs a clean run. Decisive, runs in seconds, needs no 240K prompt and no model weights.
- **`test_chunked_prefill_state_threading`** — vLLM never hands the kernel 240K tokens at once; chunked prefill threads `final_state` → `initial_state` across ~30 calls, so long-context correctness lives in that recurrence. Asserts one-shot ≡ chunk-threaded (exact invariant) at moderate lengths, and finiteness at 262144 with the failing token offset reported.

Interpretation:

| Result | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `leak_across_sequences` fails | Root cause found, reproducible in one kernel launch. |
| `state_threading` fails | Bug is in the chunked-prefill recurrence, not the packed batch. |
| Both pass | Triton path is clean; next isolate FlashKDA in prod via `additional_config: {"kda_prefill_backend": "triton"}`. |

Caveat: test inputs are `randn`, not real activations — a pass narrows the search but does not clear the kernel. (We will attach the test diff and results once a GPU run completes; contributors with A100/H100 access can run them sooner.)

# Still to check

`kda_metadata.py`'s `_get_aligned_state_indices_kernel` computes the state slot as `(seq_lens - 1) // block_size` with **no upper-bound mask against the block-table width**, then reads `first_state_slot + state_slots` for `1 + num_speculative_blocks` columns. Only reachable with `mamba_cache_mode == "align"`; set aside because prefix caching appeared off (0.0% hit rate). Would help to confirm what `mamba_cache_mode` and `max_num_batched_tokens` resolve to in a production startup log.

# Test-coverage gap contributing here

Current KDA kernel tests (`tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py:121-129`) max out at **8,192 tokens**, and the largest packed multi-sequence case is **1,200 tokens across 4 sequences**. Production ran ~240,000 tokens across 8 concurrent sequences (~29× the longest tested length, 200× the largest packed batch) — and packed multi-sequence is exactly where cross-request contamination would live. Coverage should be extended together with the root-cause fix.

# Operator mitigations available today (no vLLM change)

- Pass `repetition_detection` per request from the client — degenerate loops terminate with `FinishReason.REPETITION` within dozens of tokens.
- Set `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS=1` and alert on `vllm:corrupted_requests > 0`/`num_nans_in_logits`; on the MRV2 runner this is a Triton kernel + async D2H copy, no per-step stall (the v1 runner does a blocking `.cpu()` at `gpu_model_runner.py:5738`).
- #51036 (open) makes `repetition_detection` settable as a server-side default via `--override-generation-config`.

# Related

- #50002 — abort all in-flight requests on detected NaN logits (would reduce exposure; gated behind `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS`, default off).
- #45060 — prior fix establishing all-NaN logits as a real engine state.
- #50682 — Kimi-K3 ROCm tracking (different platform, FYI).
- #51036 — server-side `repetition_detection` default (containment, not root cause).

items.title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Tolerate NaN-corrupted logprobs in engine-core
items.body:
## Purpose

Fix a total-outage bug in the Rust frontend's engine-core client: a single request asking for `logprobs`/`prompt_logprobs` while the model produces NaN logits permanently kills the client — `/health` returns 503 and every subsequent request (including ones with no logprobs) fails with `engine-core error: messagepack ext value decode failed: token_ranks must be >= 1 for decoded engine-core logprobs` until process restart.

Rank 0 is a legitimate engine output, not a protocol violation: the sampler computes the rank as `(logprobs >= sampled_logprob).sum(-1)` (`vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py`), which is 0 when the sampled logprob is NaN because every IEEE-754 comparison against NaN is false. The decode failure is frame-scoped (one bad row fails the whole batched `EngineCoreOutputs` payload), happens on the shared output-reader path, and is recorded as a sticky health error, so a per-request data anomaly becomes a server-wide outage.

**Fix:** in `PositionLogprobs::from_decoded_row`, clamp `sampled_rank` to a minimum of 1 instead of bailing, and map non-finite logprob values to the same `-9999.0` sentinel the Python frontend uses, so a NaN state degrades to one request's model-quality problem instead of an outage.

**Why this does not duplicate existing PRs:**
- #48585 fixes the same *class* of defect (non-finite logprobs reaching the serving layer) but in the **Python** frontend, and for logprob *values*, not ranks. This PR is the Rust frontend equivalent and also covers the rank clamp it does not.
- #50725 is a different code path (process abort from an empty stop string); it only shares the blast-radius pattern.
- #50002 aborts requests on NaN detection but is gated behind `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` (default off) and does not remove this failure mode.
- #45060 establishes all-NaN logits as a real engine state vLLM already handles elsewhere.

No behavior change on any healthy payload (all pre-existing tests pass unmodified). Model evaluation N/A — this changes wire-payload decode tolerance only, not model output.

AI assistance was used for this change (fix + tests); every line has been human-reviewed. Tested with `cargo` from rustup stable 1.97.1.

## Test Plan

```bash
cd rust
cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client
```

Three new regression tests in `rust/src/engine-core-client/src/protocol/logprobs/tests.rs`:
1. `clamps_zero_sampled_rank_to_one` — `from_decoded_row` with `sampled_rank = 0` returns `Ok` with rank 1 (pins the reported bug directly).
2. `zero_sampled_rank_does_not_fail_frame_mates` — a batched `EngineCoreOutputs` frame where one request's row has rank 0 still resolves, and the *other* request's logprobs are intact (the property that matters for the outage).
3. `maps_non_finite_logprobs_to_sentinel` — NaN/±inf logprobs become `-9999.0`.

## Test Result

After the fix — all 100 package tests pass:

```
running 10 tests
test protocol::logprobs::tests::clamps_zero_sampled_rank_to_one ... ok
test protocol::logprobs::tests::maps_non_finite_logprobs_to_sentinel ... ok
test protocol::logprobs::tests::zero_sampled_rank_does_not_fail_frame_mates ... ok
... (7 pre-existing logprobs tests) ...
test result: ok. 100 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured
```

`cargo fmt -p vllm-engine-core-client -- --check` is clean.

Before the fix (same tests against unpatched `logprobs.rs`) — the 3 new tests fail, with the frame test reproducing the exact production error:

```
thread '...zero_sampled_rank_does_not_fail_frame_mates' panicked:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: ExtValueDecode { message: "token_ranks must be >= 1 for decoded engine-core logprobs" }

failures:
    protocol::logprobs::tests::clamps_zero_sampled_rank_to_one
    protocol::logprobs::tests::maps_non_finite_logprobs_to_sentinel
    protocol::logprobs::tests::zero_sampled_rank_does_not_fail_frame_mates
test result: FAILED. 7 passed; 3 failed
```

No GPU required for any of these tests.

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.

items.title: [Bug]: `BaseThinkingReasoningParser.extract_reasoning` silently discards output text when `<think>` appears mid-stream
items.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```text
vLLM:            0.25.1 (docker image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1)
Model:           poolside/Laguna-S-2.1-INT4
Flags:           --reasoning-parser poolside_v1 --tool-call-parser poolside_v1
                 --enable-auto-tool-choice
                 --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true}'
GPU:             8x RTX 3090 (SM86), TP4
```

`collect_env.py` output not attached because the deployment runs inside the
official container; the affected code path is pure Python string handling and
does not depend on hardware or backend.

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`BaseThinkingReasoningParser.extract_reasoning` drops a portion of the model's
output. The dropped text is returned in **neither** `content` **nor**
`reasoning` — it is silently lost.

Affected are parsers that inherit `BaseThinkingReasoningParser` **without**
overriding `extract_reasoning`. Checked on `main`:

| Parser | inherits base | own `extract_reasoning` | affected |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek_r1` | yes | no | **yes** |
| `poolside_v1` (via `deepseek_v3` → `deepseek_r1`) | – | no | **yes** |
| `minimax_m3` | yes | yes | no |
| `ernie45` | yes | yes | no |

#### The code

`vllm/reasoning/basic_parsers.py`, lines 157-181 on `main`:

```python
def extract_reasoning(
    self, model_output: str, request: "ChatCompletionRequest | ResponsesRequest"
) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    # Check if the start token is present in the model output, remove it
    # if it is present.
    model_output_parts = model_output.partition(self.start_token)
    model_output = (
        model_output_parts[2] if model_output_parts[1] else model_output_parts[0]
    )
    ...
```

`model_output_parts[0]` — everything **before** the matched `<think>` — is bound
to nothing. When the match succeeds, that prefix is discarded and never appears
in either return value.

The match is unanchored: `str.partition` finds the **first** occurrence anywhere
in the output. It has no notion of position, of JSON string context, or of
tool-call markup. A `<think>` the model produced as *data* is indistinguishable
from one produced as a *delimiter*.

Note this is a **string** match, so it fires regardless of tokenisation. The
model does not need to emit the reasoning special token; ordinary BPE pieces that
decode to `<think>` are enough.

#### Reproduction

Any prompt that makes a reasoning model write `<think>` in its answer will do.
Asking it to explain what the tag means is the natural case:

```bash
curl -s http://$ENDPOINT/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "'"$MODEL"'",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content":
    "Explain in two sentences what the tag consisting of a less-than sign, the letters t h i n k, and a greater-than sign means in a chat template. Write the tag out once."}],
  "max_tokens": 1200,
  "temperature": 0,
  "return_token_ids": true}'
```

Then compare the true model output against what the API returned. Detokenising
`token_ids` gives the raw generation, so nothing has to be inferred:

```python
raw = detokenize(response.token_ids)          # what the model actually produced
returned = len(content) + len(reasoning)      # what the API handed back
```

Measured, three runs at `temperature 0`:

| Run | `<think>` in raw output | raw | content | reasoning | lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | at char 680 | 2078 | 287 | 1084 | **707** |
| 2 | not written by the model | 1244 | – | – | 0 |
| 3 | at char 658 | 3805 | 364 | 2756 | **685** |

In runs 1 and 3 the first 680 / 658 characters of the reasoning are gone. Their
opening is:

```text
'Okay, the user is asking me to explain what the sequence of lowercase letters
"t h i n k" in a chat template means, and ...'
```

Verified explicitly: this text is a substring of neither `content` nor
`reasoning`. Run 2 is not a counter-example — the model simply did not write the
tag that time, so the code path was not reached.

#### Why this matters beyond the obvious

`DelegatingParser.parse` runs reasoning extraction across the **entire** raw
output before the tool-call parser gets to split arguments
(`vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py:793`):

```python
reasoning, content = self.extract_reasoning(model_output, request)
tool_calls, content = self._extract_tool_calls(content=content, ...)
```

So a `<think>` occurring inside a tool-call argument is consumed before anything
that understands tool calls has seen it. The tool parser is handed only the
remainder.

The practical failure mode is a coding agent editing source code that contains
`<think>` as a string literal — for example a chat-template or output-parser
implementation. The edit silently does nothing, or arrives truncated.

#### Affected versions

`vllm/reasoning/basic_parsers.py` is byte-identical at `v0.25.1`, `v0.26.0` and
`main` (verified by sha256). The behaviour is unchanged across all three.

#### The fix already exists in this repository

`MiniMaxM3ReasoningParser` overrides `extract_reasoning` and handles exactly this
case correctly (`vllm/reasoning/minimax_m3_reasoning_parser.py`):

```python
content_before, _, after_start = model_output.partition(self.start_token)
reasoning, end, content_after = after_start.partition(self.end_token)
if not end:
    return reasoning, content_before or None

return reasoning, (content_before + content_after) or None
```

The prefix is captured as `content_before` and concatenated onto the content
rather than dropped. Lifting this into `BaseThinkingReasoningParser` would fix
`deepseek_r1` and its delegates and let `minimax_m3` drop its override.

#### Suggested direction

Two separable problems:

1. **The discard is unambiguous data loss.** Whatever the intended semantics, a
   parser should not route text to neither output field. The `minimax_m3`
   treatment above is the obvious in-repo precedent.

2. **The unanchored search is the deeper issue.** The intent appears to be
   "strip a leading `<think>` wrapper". Anchoring the match to the start of the
   generation would express that intent and would make a mid-stream occurrence
   harmless. Parsers that moved to the `ParserEngine` design (`qwen3`,
   `glm47_moe`) do not have this problem, because a single state machine sees
   reasoning markers and tool-call markup together and knows which region of the
   stream it is in.

I am happy to open a PR for (1) if that direction is acceptable.

#### What I did not verify

- Only reproduced with `poolside_v1`. `deepseek_r1` shares the identical base
  class and the same `extract_reasoning`, so it should behave the same, but I did
  not run it.
- The streaming path (`extract_reasoning_streaming`, same file) has a separate
  single-special-token skip at lines 112-116 that also returns `None`. I have not
  characterised it and it is not part of this report.
- I have not checked whether the Rust frontend shares this logic.

#### Related but distinct

- **#48663** — `minimax_m3` splitting structured-output JSON at a `<mm:think>`
  written as data. Same *class* of problem, different parser. As shown above the
  non-streaming `minimax_m3` path preserves the prefix, so that report concerns a
  different code path.
- **#48863 / #48865** — same function, different line: misclassification of
  output that contains no think block at all (`return model_output, None` when
  `end_token` is absent). That fix does not address the discarded prefix.

### Before submitting a new issue...

items.title: [Bug]: Gemma4 tool parser (non-streaming): finish_reason=tool_calls with empty tool_calls array — model's move silently lost under concurrent load
items.body:
## Symptom

On intermittent occasions under concurrent agentic load, a **non-streaming** `/v1/chat/completions` request served with the Gemma4 tool-call parser returns:

- `choices[0].finish_reason == "tool_calls"`
- `choices[0].message.tool_calls == []` (empty array — not null, not missing)
- `choices[0].message.content` empty or a short prose echo

i.e. the engine *signals* that the model made a tool move, but the parsed calls are lost and the raw text is not surfaced either — the model's move is silently swallowed. An agentic client has nothing to execute and nothing to re-parse.

## Environment

- vLLM **0.26.0**, torch 2.11.0+cu130
- Model: `google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-w4a16-ct` (compressed-tensors W4A16; also reproduced on the 26B QAT sibling)
- 8× GPU, TP8
- Serve command:

```
vllm serve google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-w4a16-ct \
  --served-model-name nexa-small \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser gemma4 --reasoning-parser gemma4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len 131072 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
```

## Frequency / conditions

Multi-agent orchestration platform, several concurrent conversations with tool specs (10-40 tools offered per request), long prompts (10k-100k tokens). Roughly **5 occurrences over ~2 days of continuous agentic traffic** (thousands of requests) — rare, but each occurrence breaks the consuming agent's turn (we had to build a client-side typed retry barrier around it).

Client-side capture at the moment of failure (our audit layer): `finish_reason="tool_calls"`, `raw tool_calls=[]`, content head empty/echo. The same request retried immediately usually succeeds, which points at a parser/race condition rather than a prompt problem.

## Possibly related

- #39392 (Gemma4 tool-call-parser produces `<pad>` tokens under concurrent requests) — same parser, also concurrency-correlated, different visible symptom.
- #44522 (closed — parser leaked raw tokens in streaming). Ours is the non-streaming lane: nothing is leaked; the move disappears entirely.

## Expected behavior

When the Gemma4 parser cannot extract any tool call from a completion that triggered the tool-call stop condition, either (a) the raw model text should be preserved in `message.content` so the client can recover, or (b) `finish_reason` should not claim `tool_calls`. `finish_reason=tool_calls` with an empty array and empty content loses the model's output with no recovery path.

items.title: [Bugfix] MiniMax-M3 fp8_e5m2 KV cache on SM80 (A100/A800): admit the format Triton can read, fix the CUDA-graph KV corruption
items.body:
Draft port of the SM80 fp8-KV enablement for MiniMax-M3 onto current main. Fixes #50881.

**In this draft already:** the Triton attention backend guard now admits `fp8_e5m2` on SM80 — Triton there can read fp8e5; it is only fp8e4nv (e4m3) that needs SM89+. e4m3 stays rejected below SM89, and the error now suggests `fp8_e5m2` to Ampere users instead of a bf16 downgrade.

**Coming with hardware verification on 8xA800 (tomorrow):**
- route dense-layer KV writes through the CUDA `reshape_and_cache_flash` (software fp8 convert) instead of the Triton kernel that needs native fp8e4nv;
- make `MiniMaxM3SparseAttention._insert_kv` CUDA-graph-safe via `@eager_break_during_capture` — the root cause of the fp8+graph garbage diagnosed in #50881;
- the remaining SM89 guards on this path, plus needle/1M-window/GPQA numbers re-measured on main.

Diagnosis, per-kernel numerical probes, and the fork-based patch set this ports from: https://github.com/Hakureirm/minimax-m3-ampere

Marked draft until the full set and the on-hardware verification land.

items.title: [Bug]: override-generation-config silently ignores presence_penalty / frequency_penalty (missing from available_params whitelist)
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of vllm collect-env ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0 Libc version : glibc-2.35 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.11.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.13 (main, Mar 4 2026, 09:23:07) [GCC 11.4.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-28-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 GPU 1: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Nvidia driver version : 595.71.05 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 CPU(s): 44 Model name: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2696 v4 @ 2.20GHz NUMA node(s): 1 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] vllm==0.24.0 [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.12 [pip3] numpy==2.2.6 [pip3] nvidia-cublas==13.1.0.3 [pip3] nvidia-cuda-nvrtc==13.0.88 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `--override-generation-config` is intended to set server-side default sampling parameters that apply when the client does not send a value for that parameter. It works for `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `min_p`, `repetition_penalty` and `max_new_tokens`, but **silently ignores `presence_penalty` and `frequency_penalty`** — both are missing from the `available_params` whitelist in `ModelConfig.get_diff_sampling_param()` (`vllm/config/model.py`). No warning is emitted, and the sampler always falls back to `0.0`. This is the same class of silent-drop bug as #45591 (where `eos_token_id` was dropped by the same whitelist mechanism and later fixed). ```bash # Server-side default sampling params: vllm serve /path/to/model \ --generation-config vllm \ --override-generation-config '{"presence_penalty":1.5,"temperature":0.6,"top_p":0.95}' \ --enable-log-requests # Client request that does NOT send presence_penalty: curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":8}' ``` Observed server log (`--enable-log-requests`): ```text SamplingParams(... presence_penalty=0.0, ..., temperature=0.6, top_p=0.95, ...) # ^^ configured default 1.5 never applied ``` `temperature`/`top_p` from `--override-generation-config` are applied, but `presence_penalty` is not. Expected behavior: `presence_penalty` (and `frequency_penalty`) configured in `--override-generation-config` should be applied as server-side defaults, exactly like `temperature`/`top_p`. They are standard sampling parameters of both `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses`, and the only sampling parameters in this whitelist that accept a client value but have no server-default path. Root cause location: `vllm/config/model.py`, `ModelConfig.get_diff_sampling_param()`: ```python available_params = [ "repetition_penalty", "temperature", "top_k", "top_p", "min_p", "max_new_tokens", ] ``` Verified present on `v0.24.0` (this env), still present on `v0.26.0` and on `main`. Impact: deployments that rely on server-side default penalties (e.g. an LLM gateway in front of vLLM that does not forward penalty fields) cannot get presence/frequency penalty applied, causing output repetition / tool-call loops that are very hard to diagnose. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.body:
## Purpose

While building an AMD-specific variant of the performance-benchmark test configs (`serving-tests-rocm.json`, mirroring `serving-tests.json`), verifying the copied `serving_llama70B_tp4_random_128_128` entry through the actual `merge_serving_tests_stream` merge logic in `run-performance-benchmarks.sh` surfaced that its `server_parameters` never sets `tensor_parallel_size`. It silently inherits `tensor_parallel_size: 1` from the file's `defaults` block instead.

This test has presumably been running as `tp1`, not `tp4`, on the continuous `perf.vllm.ai` benchmark this whole time — the test name and the fixed 8192 `max_num_batched_tokens`/`async_scheduling` server args are set up for a 4-GPU run, but the actual TP degree silently defaulted to 1.

## Changes

- `.buildkite/performance-benchmarks/tests/serving-tests.json`: add `"tensor_parallel_size": 4` to `serving_llama70B_tp4_random_128_128`'s `server_parameters`.

## Why not duplicate

Searched open PRs touching this file. #46870 ("fix: remove stray duplicate from serving benchmark config") also touches `serving-tests.json`, but at a different, unrelated entry (`serving_llama8B_tp1_sharegpt`, ~line 28) — removes a stray duplicate JSON fragment causing invalid JSON. That PR's new `check-json` pre-commit hook validates JSON syntax only, so it wouldn't catch this bug either (this file is, and was, syntactically valid — just semantically wrong on one field). No line-range or content overlap with this change.

No open issue or PR references `serving_llama70B_tp4` or a missing `tensor_parallel_size` in this file.

## Test Plan / Result

Verified through the actual merge logic the runner script uses (`merge_serving_tests_stream`, which applies the `defaults` → per-test override merge), not just visual inspection:

```bash
# before the fix:
$ merge_serving_tests_stream tests/serving-tests.json | jq -c 'select(.test_name=="serving_llama70B_tp4_random_128_128") | .server_parameters.tensor_parallel_size'
1

# after the fix:
$ merge_serving_tests_stream tests/serving-tests.json | jq -c 'select(.test_name=="serving_llama70B_tp4_random_128_128") | .server_parameters.tensor_parallel_size'
4
```

Also confirmed:
- `jq . tests/serving-tests.json` — still valid JSON.
- All 7 test names in the file still present and merge cleanly after the change (no regression to the other entries).
- `pre-commit run --files .buildkite/performance-benchmarks/tests/serving-tests.json` passes.

---

*AI assistance disclosure: found and fixed with Claude Code, surfaced as a side effect of validating a separate AMD-specific benchmark config change against the actual merge/parsing logic in `run-performance-benchmarks.sh` rather than by inspection. I reviewed the one-line change and independently re-ran the before/after verification myself.*
